preset.name: A nor'easter up the Hudson Valley

headline.text: A nor'easter up the Hudson Valley (hypothetical): 1,492 lines down and an estimated 13.7 million people without power.

listed.label: the West Haverstraw to Yonkers 11 line
the Buchanan 1 to West Haverstraw line

root_cause.sentence: The storm cut 1,492 lines; no line went over its limit afterwards, so the whole outage is the storm's damage itself.

hospitals.assumption: A hospital counts as on backup power when the substation nearest it in the synthetic model lost at least 60% of its load. Real hospitals have their own feeders, generators and priority restoration.

assumptions.note: How long the lost load stays dark (estimated from the incident's size, a rule of thumb).
22,235 MW of customers dark for about 65.4 hours (estimated from the incident's size) at LBNL's value of lost load by customer class, weighted by U.S. sales (2024 dollars).

sources.name: LBNL, Updated Value of Service Reliability Estimates for Electric Utility Customers in the United States (Sullivan, Schellenberg & Blundell, LBNL-6941E, 2015), Table ES-1

fixes.label: Upgrade the lines
fixes.tradeoff: No line is over its limit, so an upgrade has nothing to relieve; it cannot reconnect areas cut off from supply. Engine check: no cascade, but 13.7 million people (estimate) are still without power.

no_fix.sentence: No fix exists for about 13.7 million people (estimate). Even with unlimited line capacity and no data center, the damage cuts them off from the power plants that could serve them; only rebuilding the downed lines brings them back. Every fix family was checked; none of them brings anyone back.

recovery.method_note: line limits applied: a controlled-pickup LP (generators re-dispatched, every line within its rating; loop flows not modeled)
